title: Open immersion from a ring fibre product on specified principal opens
statement: Let $B,R,R^{\prime}$ be commutative rings with identity and $s:B\to R$, $t:R^{\prime}\to R$ ring homomorphisms. Set $B^{\prime}=B\times_RR^{\prime}=\{(b,r):s(b)=t(r)\}$, with coordinatewise operations. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in R^{\prime}$ and $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in B$ satisfy $t(f_l)=s(g_l)$ and assume that each natural map $B_{g_l}\to R_{s(g_l)}$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Put $h_l=(g_l,f_l)\in B^{\prime}$ and $Q^{\prime}=\bigcup_lD_{R^{\prime}}(f_l)\subset\operatorname{Spec}R^{\prime}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then the natural maps $(B^{\prime})_{h_l}\to(R^{\prime})_{f_l}$ are isomorphisms. The restriction of $\operatorname{Spec}(B^{\prime}\to R^{\prime})$ to $Q^{\prime}$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], identifying $Q^{\prime}$ with $\bigcup_lD_{B^{\prime}}(h_l)$. These identifications use the projection homomorphisms just specified. No surjectivity of $s$ or $t$ is assumed; zero rings and empty families are allowed.

proof.text: Fix an index $l$ and abbreviate $P=B^{\prime}$, $g=g_l$, $f=f_l$, $d=s(g)=t(f)$ and $h=(g,f)$. Let $p:P\to B$ and $q:P\to R^{\prime}$ be the projections. Regard $B$, $R^{\prime}$ and $R$ as $P$-modules via $p$, $q$ and $s\circ p=t\circ q$. The maps $u:P\to B\oplus R^{\prime}$, $u(b,r)=(b,r)$, and $v:B\oplus R^{\prime}\to R$, $v(b,r)=s(b)-t(r)$, are $P$-linear. For $v$, linearity follows from $s(p(a))=t(q(a))$ for $a\in P$. The map $u$ is injective and its image is exactly $\ker(v)$ by the defining equality for $P$. Thus $0\to P\xrightarrow{u}B\oplus R^{\prime}\xrightarrow{v}R$ is exact at $P$ and at $B\oplus R^{\prime}$; no assertion of surjectivity onto $R$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 01Z8 (lemma-diagram-localize), proof: exact sequence of fibre-product modules

proof.text: Localize these two exact pairs of $P$-modules at $T=\{1,h,h^2,\ldots\}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. The $T$-localizations of $B$, $R^{\prime}$ and $R$ identify respectively with $B_g$, $(R^{\prime})_f$ and $R_d$: the fraction maps are $b/h^n\mapsto b/g^n$, $r/h^n\mapsto r/f^n$ and $a/h^n\mapsto a/d^n$. They are bijections because $h$ acts on the three modules by $g,f,d$, so their fraction equivalence relations coincide with [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Also $(B\oplus R^{\prime})_h\cong B_g\oplus(R^{\prime})_f$ by $(b,r)/h^n\mapsto(b/g^n,r/f^n)$; the inverse sends $(b/g^n,r/f^k)$ to $(g^{N-n}b,f^{N-k}r)/h^N$ for $N=\max(n,k)$. Equality of fractions verifies these formulas. The localized maps are therefore $P_h\to B_g\oplus(R^{\prime})_f$, induced by $p,q$, and $(x,z)\mapsto s_g(x)-t_f(z)$, where $s_g,t_f$ are the induced localization maps. Exactness at the first term makes the first map injective, and exactness at the middle makes its image precisely the pairs with $s_g(x)=t_f(z)$. Since it is also a ring homomorphism by coordinatewise operations, it identifies $P_h$ as a ring with $B_g\times_{R_d}(R^{\prime})_f$, compatibly with both projections.

By hypothesis $s_g:B_g\to R_d$ is a ring isomorphism. Projection $B_g\times_{R_d}(R^{\prime})_f\to(R^{\prime})_f$ is consequently a ring isomorphism with inverse $z\mapsto(s_g^{-1}(t_f(z)),z)$. Indeed this pair satisfies the fibre-product equality, its second coordinate is $z$, and for every compatible pair $(x,z)$ the first coordinate is forced to be $s_g^{-1}(t_f(z))$. Composing with step 2 gives an isomorphism $q_h:P_h\to(R^{\prime})_f$ whose formula on fractions is $(b,r)/h^n\mapsto r/f^n$. This is exactly the natural map specified in the statement. The argument applies to every $l$.

source.place: Tag 01Z9 (lemma-diagram), proof: cancellation of the isomorphism in the localized cartesian square

proof.text: Write $j:\operatorname{Spec}R^{\prime}\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ for $\operatorname{Spec}q$. Set $U_l=D_{R^{\prime}}(f_l)$ and $V_l=D_P(h_l)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] and [def-weil-open-immersion], the canonical maps from $\operatorname{Spec}(R^{\prime})_{f_l}$ and $\operatorname{Spec}P_{h_l}$ identify them as schemes with $U_l$ and $V_l$, respectively. Contravariant functoriality of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] sends the ring isomorphism of step 3 to a scheme isomorphism $U_l\xrightarrow{\sim}V_l$. It is the restriction of $j$: on rings the square commutes because $q_{h_l}((b,r)/1)=r/1$, so its two composites from $P$ coincide. Moreover $j^{-1}(V_l)=U_l$: at a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R^{\prime}$, $h_l\notin q^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$ is equivalent to $q(h_l)=f_l\notin\mathfrak p$. Thus $j|_{U_l}$, considered as a map into $\operatorname{Spec}P$, is an open immersion with image exactly $V_l$.

Restrict $j$ to $Q^{\prime}=\bigcup_lU_l$, and denote it by $j_Q$. Its underlying map is injective: if $x,y\in Q^{\prime}$ have the same image, choose $l$ with $x\in U_l$. Their common image lies in $V_l$, hence $y\in U_l$ by the inverse-image equality in step 4, and $x=y$ by the injectivity of $U_l\xrightarrow{\sim}V_l$. Every point of $Q^{\prime}$ lies in such an open $U_l$, and each composite $U_l\to Q^{\prime}\xrightarrow{j_Q}\operatorname{Spec}P$ is an open immersion by step 4. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-injective-local-source] to conclude that $j_Q$ is an open immersion. Its image is $\bigcup_lV_l$, since each $U_l$ maps onto $V_l$, giving the claimed identification. All maps are the original projection maps. If the family is empty, the same criterion has an injective empty underlying map and a vacuous local hypothesis, so it still applies. Zero rings or zero localization elements cause no change in the fraction calculations or in the empty principal opens.
